units.text: INT. FARMHOUSE KITCHEN - EVENING
A big square table, worn pale by decades of elbows.
A pot of soup on the stove, forgotten.
A rotary phone on the wall.
The window shows a field gone blue with dusk.

CORDELIA ASHWORTH, 58, the elder sister, ironing a tablecloth with slow, deliberate strokes, watches her younger sister MAEVE ASHWORTH, 54, who sits at the far end of the table with a suitcase already packed beside her chair, her coat folded neatly across her lap.
The iron hisses.
Cordelia reaches the corner of the cloth, smooths it, folds it once, and begins another pass.
You don't have to go tonight.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: The bus leaves at nine.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: There's a bus at six tomorrow.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I'd rather not wait.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Cordelia sets the iron down on its heel.
Crosses to the stove.
Lifts the lid on the soup and stirs, not tasting.
Mother's will is in the drawer. You haven't looked at it.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I don't need to.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: It says the house is ours.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: It says the house is yours. I've read it.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: You said you hadn't.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I lied.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: Cordelia puts the spoon down so softly it doesn't clink.
She wipes her hands on her apron, one finger at a time, then turns, and for a long moment looks at her sister's face, the tight jaw, the rim of red around the eyes that Maeve will not let fall.

She was always the stubborn one, and she is stubborn now, and she is leaving the way she did at eighteen, with her coat on her lap and her chin high, and Cordelia knows that if she says what she wants to say she will shatter the entire table, so she picks up the iron again.
Then go.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: That's it?
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: What did you want?
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I wanted you to say stay.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: I did. Twice.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: You said I didn't have to go.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: That's the same thing.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: It's not. It's never been the same thing.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: She stands.
Lifts the suitcase.
Holds it with both hands, like something borne from a flood.
Goodbye, Cordie.
units.name: MAEVE

units.text: The nickname lands.
Cordelia's hand tightens on the iron.
A thin trail of steam rises, curling past her face.
Behind her the soup begins to boil over, hissing on the burner.
She doesn't turn.
Don't let the door slam.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Maeve closes the door gently behind her.
The latch clicks.
Cordelia lets the iron fall onto the tablecloth.
The smell of scorched cotton rises.
She stands there, watching it burn.
